finding: Valgrind scheduler starvation in the reproduced four-worker benchmark
status: confirmed: Linux arm64 and amd64 reproductions, pure-C reproducer, three fair-scheduler repeats, all 12 benchmarks through the actual CodSpeed action
mechanism: Measured run leaves worker 0 polling Timely scheduling/progress while other workers park.
The default generic Valgrind scheduler uses a pipe-token BigLock with no fairness guarantee.
The polling worker repeatedly reacquires BigLock while timed waiters remain blocked in the internal pipe read.
Default simulation times out; changing only --fair-sched=yes uses the Linux ticket lock and completes.
Disabling CPython perf trampolines does not resolve the hang.
A minimal C program without Python or Bytewax reproduces the same waiter starvation.
notes: Durations are end-to-end diagnostic process durations, including two benchmark executions and instrumentation overhead; not production speedup.
Original multi-hour run was canceled without stacks; causality comes from bounded reproductions of the same workload.
The existing simulation/walltime split on main-upstream-clone has been preserved.
The fairness flag is experimental in CodSpeed runner 5.5.0. Walltime remains needed to measure real multi-core throughput.
A 20-second faulthandler dump appears in the successful 28-second diagnostic repeats; this is a diagnostic timer, not a test failure or supervisor timeout.
